answer: An identity counts only when three of five issuers — bank, employer, university, telecom, government — each bind a zero-knowledge uniqueness proof to one key. Forging a clone means passing three KYC rails, so attacker cost climbs like a canyon wall with each fake, about $40–$150 and days of friction each. Issuers cross-check nullifier sets each epoch, revoke duplicates and slash their bonds, while an ocean of real credentials makes a whisper of fraud stand out. Limits: people without three issuers are excluded, and a cartel could mint identities, so the set rotates and audits stay public.
